business_problem: Multiversity wanted to reinforce its leadership in educational innovation, but it needed to prove that generative AI could answer students accurately and improve staff efficiency before scaling the technology across its programs.
solution_summary: Multiversity partnered with Bain to identify more than 30 innovation initiatives and then put generative AI into production through two concrete pilots. The first, the AI University Chatbot, uses Open AI technology and class content as its knowledge base to answer student questions, clarify concepts, point students to reference sources, and provide instant feedback around the clock. The second is a custom internal tool that helps teaching staff complete administrative work much faster. Together, the deployments created a student-support and staff-efficiency architecture in which course materials are ingested into the chatbot, student prompts are served through the assistant, and teaching tasks flow through a separate operational tool. The source does not identify a dedicated storage platform, but it is explicit that the chatbot is already active in many courses and that professors validated the assistant's accuracy before broader use.

data_flow: Class contents feed the AI University Chatbot, which serves 24/7 responses, clarifications, and references to students. A separate custom tool handles staff administrative workflows, turning operational inputs into faster task completion for teaching teams.
business_outcome: Multiversity put generative AI into live teaching support with very high measured accuracy and student satisfaction, while also speeding staff administration enough to free educators for more valuable work.
